belongs_to: Section 6.4, "Method 4" (after Methods 1-3): the circle pattern with the labels "Step 1 Step 2 Step 3 Step 4 ... Step k" and the expressions 1 x 3 = 1 x (1 + 2), 2 x 4 = 2 x (2 + 2), 3 x 5 = 3 x (3 + 2), 4 x 6 = 4 x (4 + 2), ..., k x (k+2)
description: One row, left to right: four drawn steps, then a dotted ellipsis '. . .' at mid height of the figures, then the label 'Step k' with NO drawing under it. Above every drawing a label: 'Step 1', 'Step 2', 'Step 3', 'Step 4', '. . .', 'Step k' (the step numbers are bold blue, k is italic blue). Circles are solid black, all the same size, touching their neighbours in a square grid, and they are enclosed in thin dark-red (maroon) rectangles. All four drawings are top-aligned. Rule for Step k (k = 1..4): the drawing has k+1 rows; the first k columns hold k+1 circles each and sit in ONE maroon rectangle (k columns wide, k+1 rows tall); one more column of k circles sits to the right of that rectangle, top-aligned, in its own maroon rectangle (1 column wide, k rows tall); so the bottom-right position is empty and the bottom row has k circles. Counted: Step 1 = 3 circles (left rectangle 1 wide x 2 tall = 2 circles, right rectangle 1 x 1 = 1 circle at the top; rows of 2 and 1). Step 2 = 8 circles (left rectangle 2 x 3 = 6, right rectangle 1 x 2 = 2; rows of 3, 3, 2). Step 3 = 15 circles (left rectangle 3 x 4 = 12, right rectangle 1 x 3 = 3; rows of 4, 4, 4, 3). Step 4 = 24 circles (left rectangle 4 x 5 = 20, right rectangle 1 x 4 = 4; rows of 5, 5, 5, 5, 4). Under each drawing two lines of text: first line in dark red '1 x 3', '2 x 4', '3 x 5', '4 x 6'; second line '= 1 x (1 + 2)', '= 2 x (2 + 2)', '= 3 x (3 + 2)', '= 4 x (4 + 2)' (the repeated step numbers are bold blue); under the ellipsis another '. . .'; under 'Step k' the single line 'k x (k+2)' with k in italic blue.

Labels (italic, with double-headed arrows): 'm' above a short horizontal double arrow placed over the top-left rectangle, spanning exactly its width (the left rectangle's width); 'n' to the right of a long vertical double arrow along the right side, spanning the length of the right rectangle (from the bottom edge of the top rectangle to the bottom of the figure). description: Three steps printed side by side, left to right, with the text 'Step 1', 'Step 2', 'Step 3' printed below each drawing (all on the same baseline). Basic unit = one small square cell with pale yellow fill (about #FAF28C) and a thin dark outline; cells touch, all the same size in all steps. Every step is a Z / S shape: a solid rectangular block in the middle, a column of cells hanging DOWN from the block's LEFT column, and a column of cells rising UP from the block's RIGHT column. The bottoms of the three blocks are on the same level. Counted by pixel measurement: Step 1: block 3 wide x 1 tall (3 cells); 3 more cells below its left cell; 3 more cells above its right cell; left column 4 cells tall in total, right column 4 cells tall in total; total 3 + 3 + 3 = 9 cells. Step 2: block 4 wide x 2 tall (8 cells); 4 more cells below the left column; 4 more cells above the right column (left and right columns 6 cells tall each in total); total 8 + 4 + 4 = 16 cells. Step 3: block 5 wide x 3 tall (15 cells); 6 more cells below the left column; 6 more cells above the right column (left and right columns 9 cells tall each in total); total 15 + 6 + 6 = 27 cells.
unclear: The printed arm lengths are 3, 4, 6 (cells above the right column / below the left column) for Steps 1, 2, 3, so the drawn totals are 9, 16, 27. A smooth rule (arms 3, 4, 5, i.e. n + 2) would give 9, 16, 25, which is what the printed answer on pdf p.34 uses ((2 + n)^2). The drawing as printed has 6 cells in the Step 3 arms (counted from the pixels of the page picture); decide how to draw it from the question, not from this count.
